summary: LTP and Quote clients on one NSE equity: the Quote client moves the subscription up (a POST of 1501, then a PUT of the LTP code once the broker took it), and a 1105 text event (t:1_2885,110:...,119:...) arrives. Jainam's adapter publishes it to every held mode in that mode's dict, its counts as doubles (float()): the desktop reads it as the touchline its codes 110-119 are, so under Jainam's per-mode fold the LTP client gets the LTP dict and the Quote client the Quote dict.

notes: 1105 carries the touchline codes 110-119 (families/xts/binary.rs parse_1105); it has no MessageCode and no trade time, so the frames carry no ltt.

The Jainam web client marks it 1512, but its adapter publishes every message to every mode the symbol's subscriptions hold, in that mode's dict (jainamxts_adapter.py _process_json_data), so the code picks no topic: the desktop reads it as a touchline (XtsHooks::text_1105_as_ltp off) and sends each holder its mode's frame, the counts as doubles (XtsHooks::text_1105_doubles, NumberForm::Double).

The desktop holds one subscription per instrument at the highest mode its clients ask for (websocket::manager), so the Quote client changes the LTP subscription into a Quote one; the web adapter subscribes each mode on its own.

deviations.reason: The event carries no trade time; the web sends ltt 0 (.get('LastTradedTime', 0)), the desktop leaves ltt out (docs: a field the stream does not carry is left out; never a receipt time passed off as a trade time).
The web's server also sends this client a richer mode's publication of the instrument, beyond the modes it holds; the desktop sends one frame per held mode.
deviations.ref: websocket_proxy/server.py zmq_listener (for m in range(1, mode + 1))
